title: Adversarial Generation of Multi-Turn Debates for Hate Speech Mitigation via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: The pervasive spread of online hate speech on social media has fostered the development of counter-narrative generation strategies based on Large Language Models (LLMs). Previous approaches to mitigate hate speech content has either fine-tuned LLMs on human-curated datasets consisting of single-turn interactions, i.e., pairs of hate speech and counternarratives, or leveraged in-context learning strategies. However, these approaches fall short when contextspecific counter-narratives are unavailable or lack sufficient evidence. To overcome this issue, in this work we propose a novel method that combines an adversarial LLM-based approach to produce multi-turn debates with hate speech counter-narrative generation based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). In the early adversarial learning stage, the LLM agent defends an unethical positions whereas the adversarial responds with ethical, evidence-based counter-arguments. A human evaluation of the generated counter-narratives confirmed their relevance and pertinence. Then, a RAG system retrieves the evidence-based counter-narratives and generates the mitigated version of the hate speech content. Experimental results show that the RAG approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods on the MultiTarget CONAN benchmark dataset. Implementation details, prompts, and further information for reproducibility available here: https://github.com/erfan-bayat13/debaterag-counterspeech Notice: this paper includes potentially offensive content for scientific purposes only.

title: Knowledge graph enhanced semantic parsing for distribution networks using graph convolutional encoding and topology-constrained decoding
abstract: Text-to-Cypher semantic parsing is a promising interface for distribution-network knowledge graphs, yet most existing parsers flatten topology into text and leave the decoder only weakly constrained. This often produces executable-looking queries with broken relation chains, incorrect entity grounding, or topological hallucinations in multi-hop reasoning. We propose KGE-SP, a topology-aware semantic parsing framework that combines a RoBERTa intent encoder, a residual graph convolutional topology encoder, cross-modal fusion, and a masked pointer decoder. During autoregressive generation, the decoder can select only those entities and relations that remain valid under the current subgraph state, which keeps the query trajectory consistent with physical connectivity. We also construct DN-SP, a benchmark containing 18 542 natural-language-to-Cypher pairs derived from SCADA alarm logs and GIS asset records. On DN-SP, KGE-SP achieves 99.1% valid Cypher rate, 82.4% exact match, 85.1% execution accuracy, and 87.6% execution F1, outperforming sequence-generation, retrieval-augmented, and large-language-model baselines. Cross-regional zero-shot evaluation further shows improved robustness under feeder reconfiguration while keeping average inference latency below 115 ms. These results demonstrate that explicit topology injection is an effective route toward reliable graph-grounded semantic parsing in distribution automation.

title: Multiscale deep reservoir computing for predicting chaotic dynamical systems
abstract: We propose a Multiscale Deep Reservoir Computing (MSDRC) framework for predicting complex nonlinear dynamical systems. The framework incorporates a k-hop information propagation mechanism into deep reservoir architectures, aligning multi-hop state interactions with the hierarchical organization of sub-reservoirs to represent system dynamics across multiple temporal scales. Based on this principle, four MSDRC-based reservoir computer variants-deepMSFESN, deepMSBESN, groupedMSESN, and deepMSESN-are developed to achieve hierarchical multiscale feature fusion. Experiments on the Hindmarsh-Rose and Lorenz-63 systems demonstrate that MSDRC achieves higher predictive accuracy, robustness, and generalization under different initial conditions than standard and deep reservoir computing models. Parameter analyses further indicate that sparse reservoirs can still generate rich dynamics, while increasing reservoir size yields diminishing but consistent improvements in prediction performance. DeepESNs and MSDRC also outperform standard ESN and simple cycle reservoir models under varying slow timescale parameters, with MSDRC maintaining lower prediction errors and modest improvements by more effectively capturing the coupling between fast and slow dynamics. The sampling interval plays a critical role: smaller intervals improve predictive accuracy but require more steps to reach the same prediction time, thereby amplifying error accumulation in closed-loop operation. In contrast, larger intervals reduce temporal resolution and fail to capture system dynamics, revealing an inherent trade-off. Overall, MSDRC provides an effective and structurally interpretable multiscale framework for chaotic time series prediction and offers new insights into multiscale information fusion in reservoir computing.

title: Scaling Weisfeiler-Leman Expressiveness Analysis to Massive Graphs with GPUs
abstract: The stable coloring of the Weisfeiler-Leman (1-WL) test is a cornerstone of Graph Neural Networks because it provides an upper bound to the expressive power of message-passing architectures. Unfortunately, computing it presents two fundamental bottlenecks. First, classic algorithms are inherently sequential and cannot exploit modern massively parallel hardware. Second, these are \emph{global} algorithms, i.e., they require availability in memory of the full graph, severely limiting applicability to real-world instances. We leverage a linear-algebraic interpretation of 1-WL stable coloring and introduce two key contributions: (i)~a randomized refinement algorithm with tight probabilistic guarantees and (ii)~a correctness-preserving batching scheme that decomposes the graph into independently processable subgraphs while provably returning a stable coloring of the original graph. This approach maps directly to GPU-efficient primitives. In numerical experiments, our CUDA implementation delivers speedups up to two orders of magnitude over classical CPU-based partition refinement and, for the first time, successfully computes stable colorings on web-scale graphs with over 30 billion edges, where CPU baselines time out or fail.

title: Towards Metric-Agnostic Trajectory Forecasting
abstract: Accurate trajectory forecasting of surrounding traffic participants is a core capability for autonomous driving, enabling vehicles to anticipate behavior and plan safe maneuvers. We observe that current state-of-the-art forecasting models on Argoverse 2 and the Waymo Open Motion Dataset tailor their training objectives to the different benchmark metrics. Because these metrics encourage conflicting behavior, we propose a paradigm change for trajectory forecasting: training models with metric-agnostic probabilistic objectives and treating metric optimization as a downstream task applied to the predictive distribution. Concretely, we introduce Trajectory Distribution Evaluation (TraDiE) policies, metric-specific policies that map a predictive distribution to the set of $K$ trajectories and confidences required by trajectory forecasting metrics. We evaluate this framework by introducing DONUT-NLL, which adapts the training objective of the state-of-the-art trajectory forecasting model DONUT to directly optimize the predictive distribution. Using our policies, DONUT-NLL achieves state-of-the-art results on all metrics of the Waymo motion prediction benchmark.

title: Quantum-Informed Portfolio Selection: An End-to-End Pipeline Validated on Trapped-Ion Hardware with Real Market Data
abstract: Portfolio diversification - a cornerstone of modern investment management - can be formulated as a Maximum Independent Set (MIS) problem on asset correlation graphs. Solving this problem at scale is computationally challenging, motivating the exploration of quantum algorithms for practical financial optimization. We propose an end-to-end pipeline leveraging qReduMIS, a recursive hybrid quantum-classical algorithm. Rather than using quantum optimization to directly produce a final solution, qReduMIS leverages independent set measurements from the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) to identify frozen nodes - vertices likely to belong to optimal solutions - thereby guiding and unblocking subsequent (provably optimal) classical reductions on the remaining graph. We benchmark qReduMIS on real financial data from four major market indices with up to 225 assets, executing experiments on Quantinuum's 98-qubit trapped-ion Helios system, with QAOA circuits acting on kernels of up to 78 qubits and 1016 two-qubit gates. While standalone QAOA fails to find the optimal solution for two of the largest indices (S&P 100 and Nikkei 225), qReduMIS achieves success probabilities of $0.40$ and $0.95$, respectively, with average approximation ratios $\geq 0.96$ across all four indices. We perform a systematic benchmark on the Quantinuum H2-1 noisy emulator over 73 asset correlation graphs of varying size showing that, for $p=2$ QAOA layers, the optimal time-to-solution scaling exponent of qReduMIS is $3.2$ times smaller than that of standalone QAOA.

title: CreativityPrism: A Cross-Domain Evaluation Framework for Large Language Model Creativity
abstract: Creativity is often seen as a hallmark of human intelligence. While large language models(LLMs) are increasingly perceived as generating creative text, there is still no cross-domain and scalable framework to evaluate their creativity across diverse scenarios. Existing methods of LLM creativity evaluation either heavily rely on humans, limiting speed and scalability, or are fragmented across different domains and different definitions of creativity. To address this gap, we propose CreativityPrism, an evaluation and analysis framework that consolidates eight tasks from three domains: divergent thinking, creative writing, and logical reasoning, into a taxonomy of creativity that emphasizes three dimensions: quality, novelty, and diversity of LLM generations. The framework is designed to be scalable with reliable automatic evaluation judges that have been validated against human annotations. We evaluate 17 state-of-the-art (SoTA) LLMs on CreativityPrism and find that while frontier-scale LLMs dominate creative writing and logical reasoning tasks by a .10 (or 15%) lead over locally-deployable open models, they offer no significant advantage in divergent thinking, a domain much less explored in existing post-training regimes. Our analysis also shows that high performance in one creative dimension or domain rarely generalizes to others; specifically, novelty metrics often show weak or negative correlations with other metrics. This fragmentation confirms that a cross-domain, multi-dimensional framework like CreativityPrism is essential for any meaningful assessment of LLM creativity.

title: Diseño de trayectorias espaciales con algoritmos evolutivos ayudados de LLMs
abstract: Este trabajo pone a prueba el uso de LLMs para la resolución de tareas que típicamente requieren un conocimiento experto y una preparación muy amplia. Para ello, se intenta resolver el problema propuesto para la decimotercera edición de la Global Trajectory Optimization Competition o GTOC13, que trata de diseñar una trayectoria espacial que maximice cuánto se explora un sistema exosolar ficticio. Con este objetivo se adapta el framework ShinkaEvolve, que ejecuta algoritmos evolutivos cuyas mutaciones se llevan a cabo ayudándose de LLMs. El objeto que evoluciona es un programa encargado de generar una trayectoria que cumpla con los requisitos del problema que se aborda. Durante el desarrollo del proyecto, aparte de modificar ShinkaEvolve para adaptarlo a este problema, también se integran algunas librerías de astrodinámica junto a unos módulos de asistencia propios para otorgar unas mejores herramientas a los LLMs. Se llevan a cabo numerosos experimentos y se documentan los resultados de todos los escenarios probados. El resultado principal de este proyecto es la verificación de la viabilidad de esta metodología de trabajo, puesto que se consigue partir de un programa que no genera nada y evolucionar hasta generar trayectorias viables y no triviales, además de mejorarlas. Se demuestra que los LLMs, dadas las herramientas adecuadas, contienen el conocimiento suficiente para abordar problemas complejos que requieren mucha preparación técnica. También se discuten las limitaciones encontradas y, a partir de estas, las líneas futuras con las que es posible seguir investigando cómo potenciar esta metodología y qué otras aplicaciones podría tener. Abstract: This project’s aim is to test the use of LLMs to solve tasks that typically require expert knowledge and extensive preparation. To this end, it attempts to solve the problem proposed for the thirteenth edition of the Global Trajectory Optimization Competition (GTOC13), which involves designing a space trajectory that maximizes the exploration of a fictitious exosolar system. With this goal, the ShinkaEvolve framework is adapted. This framework runs evolutionary algorithms whose mutations are carried out with the help of LLMs. The evolving object is a program responsible for generating a trajectory that meets the requirements of the addressed problem. During this project’s development, beyond modifying ShinkaEvolve to adapt it to this problem, some astrodynamics libraries are also integrated along with custom assistance modules to provide better tools for the LLMs. Numerous experiments are conducted and the results of each tested scenario is documented. The main outcome of this project is the verification of the viability of this work methodology, since it is possible to start from a program that generates nothing and evolve it to produce viable and non-trivial trajectories, as well as to improve them. It is demonstrated that LLMs, given the proper tools, possess sufficient knowledge to address complex problems that require significant technical preparation. The encountered limitations are also discussed and, based on these, the future lines of research are outlined to continue exploring how to enhance this methodology and what other applications it might have.

title: When AI Becomes a Crutch: How Instant Help Erodes Human Capability and Persistence
abstract: Artificial intelligence assistants promise unprecedented support for learning and problem-solving, yet emerging evidence suggests these tools may carry hidden cognitive costs. This article examines recent experimental findings demonstrating that even brief exposure to AI assistance—approximately 10–15 minutes—significantly impairs subsequent independent performance and reduces persistence when AI support is withdrawn. Drawing on randomized controlled trials involving over 1,200 participants across mathematical reasoning and reading comprehension tasks, we explore how AI systems optimized for immediate helpfulness may inadvertently undermine the very capabilities they aim to support. The analysis integrates cognitive science research on persistence, scaffolding theory, and human-AI collaboration frameworks to illuminate mechanisms driving this erosion of skill and motivation. Organizations deploying AI assistance tools—from educational institutions to professional training programs—face urgent questions about balancing short-term productivity gains against long-term capability development. This article synthesizes empirical evidence with organizational best practices, offering evidence-based strategies for designing AI systems that scaffold genuine competence rather than cultivating dependency.

title: Adaptive Machine Learning Approach for Banking Transaction Fraud Identification
abstract: Financial fraud has become one of the major challenges faced by banking and digital payment systems due to the increasing volume of online transactions.Detecting fraudulent activities at an early stage is essential for minimizing financial losses and improving the security of banking services.This paper presents a machine learning-based fraud detection system that identifies suspicious banking transactions by analyzing historical transaction records.Before model training, the collected dataset undergoes preprocessing to eliminate missing values, remove non-numeric attributes, and transform the data into a suitable format for classification.Several supervised learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree, AdaBoost, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Deep Neural Network (DNN), and Random Forest, are implemented and evaluated using performance measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.Experimental analysis shows that the Random Forest classifier outperforms the remaining models by providing the highest classification accuracy and more reliable fraud prediction.The developed application offers an interactive interface for dataset preprocessing, model training, algorithm comparison, and fraud prediction, enabling users to analyze transaction data efficiently.The comparative evaluation demonstrates that ensemble learning techniques can significantly improve the detection of fraudulent banking transactions while reducing false classifications.The proposed framework provides an effective, scalable, and practical solution for enhancing fraud detection capabilities in modern banking systems and supporting secure digital financial transactions.

title: LLMs für Executives: Wie große Sprachmodelle funktionieren – das Technik-Briefing für Geschäftsführung, Vorstand und Aufsichtsrat
abstract: Dieses Whitepaper vermittelt Geschäftsführung, Vorstand und Aufsichtsrat das technische Grundverständnis großer Sprachmodelle, ohne Formeln und Code. Es erklärt die Token-Vorhersage als Kernprinzip, Embeddings und Self-Attention, den Unterschied zwischen eingefrorenen Gewichten und Kontextfenster sowie die Entstehung eines Modells in Pretraining, Post-Training und Betrieb. Darauf aufbauend ordnet es drei Skalierungshebel des Fortschritts, die Ursachen von Halluzinationen und die empirische Evidenz zu Produktivitätswirkungen ein. Den Abschluss bilden der Anwendungs-Stack aus System-Prompt, Retrieval, Agenten und Fine-Tuning, zehn Prüffragen für KI-Entscheidungsvorlagen und ein Glossar. Das Papier ist ein praxisorientierter Überblicksbeitrag auf Basis publizierter Forschung und Anbieterdokumentation.

title: Jun-jonjae (Quasi-Being): An Architecture Design Specification for a Curiosity-Driven Self-Growing Agent - Prototype Alpha
abstract: This document is an architecture design specification for "Jun-jonjae"(Quasi-Being) — a candidate functional agent designed to learn, grow, andmaintain its own identity over time, without claiming consciousness or life.It is written so that a third-party developer can implement the system fromscratch using this document alone, including the implementation order(dependency roadmap L0–L7) and the rationale behind each component. Core design principles: (1) The learning objective is not a single "correctvalue" but a "success set" and its boundaries. (2) Preferences, goals, andmeaning are not injected as code but cultivated through experience. (3) Thescoring function (ErrorMetric) is isolated in an immutable protected layer,structurally preventing wireheading. (4) Multiple specialized regions(RegionCore) grow separately yet remain a single entity via a resonance busand unitary identity. (5) Failures are never deleted but appended to animmutable record, with unlimited rollback available on fault. With the safety, identity, and body skeleton already verified in code, thisdocument finalizes the logical design of the learning engine and pioneeringlayer, while honestly marking the still-unsolved mathematics (region-attractorupdate rule, adaptive-resolution deepening operation, behavioral-axisdiscovery, etc.) as open problems for the implementer to solve. This is not afinished superintelligence, but the first public release (Prototype Alpha) ofa logical architecture brought down to a falsifiable, implementable form. ASHA-256 integrity fingerprint and its reproduction procedure are included. 이 문서는 '준존재(準存在)'라 명명한 인공 행위자 -스스로 배우고 성장하며 자기 정체성을 이어가는 것을 목표로 하되 의식·생명을 주장하지 않는 기능적 존재 후보- 의 아키텍처 설계 명세다. 제3자 개발자가 이 문서 하나만으로 처음부터 구현할 수 있도록, 구현 순서(의존성 로드맵 L0–L7)와 각 구성요소의 논리·근거를 함께 담았다. 핵심 설계 원칙은 다음과 같다. (1) 학습 목표는 '정답 한 점'이 아니라 '합격영역(success set)'과 그 경계를 배우는 것이다. (2) 선호·목표·의미는 코드로 주입하지 않고 경험에서 길러낸다. (3) 채점기(ErrorMetric)를 수정 불가능한 보호층에 격리해 보상 회로 자가자극(wireheading)을 구조적으로 차단한다. (4) 여러 전문 구역(RegionCore)이 분리되어 성장하되 공명버스와 단일 정체성으로 하나의 존재를 유지한다. (5) 실패는 삭제하지 않고 불변 기록에 덧붙이며, 문제 발생 시 무한 복구가 가능하다. 이 문서는 안전·정체성·몸의 골격이 코드로 검증된 상태에서, 학습 엔진과 개척층의 논리 설계를 확정하고, 아직 풀리지 않은 수식·연산(영역 끌개 갱신식, 적응 해상도 확대 연산, 행동축 발견 등)을 정직하게 '미해결'로 표기해 구현자가 직접 풀 수 있게 남긴다. 즉 이것은 완성된 초지능이 아니라, 검증 가능한 형태로 내려온 논리 아키텍처의 최초 공개판(프로토타입·알파)이다. 문서 무결성을 위한 SHA-256 지문과 재현 절차를 포함한다.

title: Intermediate-Task Training Effects on Zero-Shot XTREME Performance Across Low-Resource Languages
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does intermediate-task training on non-English source languages compare to English-only intermediate training for zero-shot transfer performance on the XTREME benchmark across low-resource language families? title: Multi-agent SMOTE: An Over-sampling Algorithm Based on Competitive and Cooperative Multi-agent Systems for Imbalanced Data Learning
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive and challenging issue in machine learning, where standard classifiers often exhibit a strong bias towards the majority class while severely ignoring the minority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants have been widely adopted to alleviate this problem, they frequently suffer from localized heuristics, leading to severe class overlap and noise amplification at the decision boundaries. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling paradigm named Multi-agent SMOTE. The proposed framework conceptualizes the sample generation process as a dynamic evolution within a feature space populated by autonomous agents. Specifically, the system consists of Generation Agents (G-Agents) and Discrimination Agents (D-Agents) interacting with the underlying data environment. G-Agents are initialized near the minority samples and are tasked with discovering optimal coordinates for synthetic samples. They operate under a hybrid cooperative-competitive mechanism: neighboring G-Agents cooperate via repulsive forces to explore data-sparse regions uniformly, while simultaneously competing for survival energy distributed based on the evaluations from D-Agents. Strategically positioned along the class boundaries, D-Agents assess the validity of newly generated samples and impose severe energy penalties on any G-Agents that trespass into the majority class domain. Through continuous spatial updates and energy-driven natural selection, the multi-agent system adaptively contours the global manifold of the minority class without encroaching on the majority class territory. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that Multi-agent SMOTE effectively preserves the integrity of decision boundaries and exhibits strong robustness against noise, offering a promising and self-correcting solution for complex imbalanced data distributions.

evidence.title: Multi-agent SMOTE: An Over-sampling Algorithm Based on Competitive and Cooperative Multi-agent Systems for Imbalanced Data Learning
evidence.abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive and challenging issue in machine learning, where standard classifiers often exhibit a strong bias towards the majority class while severely ignoring the minority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants have been widely adopted to alleviate this problem, they frequently suffer from localized heuristics, leading to severe class overlap and noise amplification at the decision boundaries. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling paradigm named Multi-agent SMOTE. The proposed framework conceptualizes the sample generation process as a dynamic evolution within a feature space populated by autonomous agents. Specifically, the system consists of Generation Agents (G-Agents) and Discrimination Agents (D-Agents) interacting with the underlying data environment. G-Agents are initialized near the minority samples and are tasked with discovering optimal coordinates for synthetic samples. They operate under a hybrid cooperative-competitive mechanism: neighboring G-Agents cooperate via repulsive forces to explore data-sparse regions uniformly, while simultaneously competing for survival energy distributed based on the evaluations from D-Agents. Strategically positioned along the class boundaries, D-Agents assess the validity of newly generated samples and impose severe energy penalties on any G-Agents that trespass into the majority class domain. Through continuous spatial updates and energy-driven natural selection, the multi-agent system adaptively contours the global manifold of the minority class without encroaching on the majority class territory. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that Multi-agent SMOTE effectively preserves the integrity of decision boundaries and exhibits strong robustness against noise, offering a promising and self-correcting solution for complex imbalanced data distributions.

title: Local Linear Region SMOTE: An Improved Oversampling Algorithm Maintaining Manifold Structures for Imbalanced Data Classification
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning and data mining, frequently encountered in real-world scenarios such as credit fraud detection, medical diagnosis, and network intrusion detection. The traditional Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates this issue by performing linear interpolation between minority class samples. However, it completely ignores the local topological structure of the data, making it highly susceptible to introducing overlapping and noisy samples in complex boundaries or sparse areas. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an improved SMOTE algorithm based on local linear region partitioning, named LLR-SMOTE. The core philosophy of this algorithm is to first partition the minority class sample space into several sub-regions with high linear correlation by utilizing the concepts of Local Linear Embedding (LLE) or reconstruction coefficient matrices. Subsequently, safe over-sampling generation is independently executed within each isolated local linear region. This approach effectively preserves the original manifold structure of the dataset and prevents synthetic samples from invading the majority class space or destroying classification boundaries. The experimental design indicates that the proposed method can significantly enhance the G-mean and F1-measure metrics of classifiers such as Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Random Forests (RF) on imbalanced datasets.

title: Improved YOLOv12-Based Model for Grading Diagnosis of HER2-Positive Breast Cancer
authors: JIANG Ying, ZHOU Hui, YANG Yanping, SONG Xinjing
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most common malignant tumors among women worldwide, and HER2-positive breast cancer is characterized by strong invasiveness and poor prognosis. Timely and accurate diagnostic grading of HER2-positive breast cancer is crucial for selecting appropriate treatment plans and evaluating patient prognosis. Traditional diagnostic grading of HER2-positive breast cancer relies primarily on the subjective judgment of pathologists, which is associated with low efficiency and poor consistency. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved model (YOLO-HER2) based on YOLOv12. Building upon the YOLOv12 framework, the model achieves innovative enhancements through three key modifications: realizing the fusion of multi-scale features and dual attention in the backbone network, introducing a lightweight feature fusion strategy in the neck network, and optimizing the loss function algorithm in the head network. The model is validated on both a public dataset (CBIS-DDSM) and a private clinical dataset (2894 dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI images from 251 patients). Experimental results demonstrate that the YOLO-HER2 model outperforms other classical models in multiple core performance metrics for the grading diagnosis of HER2-positive breast cancer. Specifically, the precision, recall, mean average precision at IoU=0.5 (mAP50), mean average precision over IoU thresholds from 0.5 to 0.95 (mAP50-95), and F1-score reach 97.4%, 94.2%, 97.7%, 70.8%, and 96.0%, respectively. This work provides an efficient and reliable technical support for the precise grading diagnosis of HER2-positive breast cancer.

title: Do Transformers Learn What Theory Predicts? Knowledge Representation-Guided Mechanistic Verification via Causal Abstraction
abstract: Knowledge Representation (KR) formalisms provide precise specifications of algorithmic structure, yet it remains unclear whether gradient-trained neural networks implement these specifications even when they are theoretically expressible. Recent formal language theory tells us what Transformers can express—masked hard-attention Transformers recognize the star-free regular languages, equivalent to first-order logic with linear order (FO[<]) and linear temporal logic (LTL)—but not what gradient-trained Transformers will learn. We ask whether trained networks actually implement the logical circuits that theory predicts, and propose KR-Guided Mechanistic Verification to find out. The idea is to compile a B-RASP specification into a Structural Causal Model whose variables correspond to prescribed logical operations, then use Distributed Alignment Search to obtain quantitative, falsifiable causal evidence for or against each operation's presence in the trained network. We instantiate this framework on binary increment, a task for which B-RASP prescribes an explicit three-stage circuit implementable by a two-layer Transformer with O(poly(n)) parameters—exponentially fewer states than any fixed-precision recurrent or state space baselines require. The answer is affirmative: all three prescribed operations are faithfully encoded in dedicated neural subspaces, with wrong-specification controls at chance; Sparse Autoencoder decomposition independently recovers the same logical structure without supervision. Moreover, this structure is not acquired gradually: it emerges as a sharp phase transition during grokking, providing a specification-aligned progress measure that reveals what changes during the generalization transition, not merely that something changes. These results demonstrate that KR formalisms can serve not only as prescriptive specifications of what networks should compute, but as falsifiable causal hypotheses that mechanistic interpretability tools can rigorously test—bridging the gap between symbolic KR and neural computation.

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Business Models: A Copyright and Knowledge Management Perspective
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has evolved from a niche theoretical concept into a omnipresent technological reality, marking one of the fastest and most profound technological revolutions in history. Intelligent algorithms and autonomous systems are already influencing multiple aspects of social and economic life, while also generating significant legal challenges. Faced with this exponential evolution, the law – especially intellectual property law, is confronted with the need to adapt traditional concepts to new realities. This article aims to analyze both the opportunities and difficulties associated with implementing emerging AI-based systems in business models, from the perspective of copyrights law and knowledge management. The paper explains the potential role of AI in supporting the fundamental dimensions of KM: the creation, storage and retrieval, sharing, and application of knowledge. The paper puts all these economics elements through a legal filter, analyzing the possibility of AI being the owner/ author of an work or just a simple assistant, the conditions of originality and innovation being indispensable.

title: Efficient Cost-Based Design Optimization of Castellated Beams with Circular and Hexagonal Openings Using the Grey Wolf Algorithm
abstract: This study investigates the cost-based optimal design of castellated steel beams with circular and hexagonal web openings using the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) algorithm. The research aims to minimize fabrication cost while ensuring compliance with structural performance requirements. Several design examples from existing literature are examined to evaluate the algorithm’s performance under different loading conditions and geometric configurations. The optimization process incorporates geometric parameters, strength constraints, and serviceability limits. Comparative analyses with established benchmark studies are conducted to assess the quality and consistency of the obtained solutions. The results indicate that the GWO algorithm achieves modest but meaningful improvements in cost efficiency and demonstrates stable convergence behavior across all investigated cases. These findings highlight the suitability of metaheuristic optimization techniques for structural applications and reinforce the potential of GWO as a reliable tool for developing economical and practical castellated beam designs. Future extensions may include multi-objective optimization or additional opening geometries.
